ai.description: This gecko reaches 7 cm in length. It features a pale brown body with dark, irregular transverse bands and a granular dorsal texture. Distinctive features include slender, non-dilated digits.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus nebulosus* is best distinguished by its distinct, irregular dark brown blotches on the back, which are separated by narrow, pale, cloud-like interspaces.
ai.habitat: *Cyrtodactylus nebulosus* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks or rocks at elevations up to 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Clouded Indian Gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging after dark to forage for small insects and invertebrates on rocky outcrops and tree trunks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cyrtodactylus nebulosus* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon and monsoon months (April–August).
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cyrtodactylus nebulosus* is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in the states of Maharashtra and Karnataka at mid-to-high elevations.
